chequeos.detalle: the fake-WiFi-HAL overlay (com.android.wifi.apex + com.android.tethering.apex + framework-res.apk, built from the project's own AOSP tree against the production Wifi.patch, mac80211_hwsim-backed) and the native jg_netfix.sh daemon are injected/launched on an UNMODIFIED official redroid/redroid:15.0.0-latest image through the module's own stage 4 (integrate) / stage 6 (ensureRuntimeReady), with no custom image build required by the user

through the real module system (POST /api/modules/wifi-interno/accept + recreate), cmd wifi status reports "Wifi is connected to 'jg-wifi'" with a real IP (/172.17.0.6) on wlan0 (eth0 renamed by jg_netfix.sh)
dumpsys connectivity shows DnsAddresses: [/8.8.8.8,/8.8.4.4], a full default route, and `ping www.google.com` resolves and replies for real (not just a raw-IP ping)

Plants vs Zombies 2 (EA/PopCap, installed via Aurora Store, see project's own notes on that path) shows real ads over this connection, after the ad SDK's normal first-fill delay -- confirms the fake connectivity is good enough for a real third-party network dependency, not just Android's own superficial internet-check

validaciones.notas: This validates the hwsim-backed wifi-interno module as an addable module on the stock official image (no custom AOSP build needed by the user). It is NOT the virt_wifi-backed alternative (wifi-interno-virtwifi module): that one remains experimental, is not part of redroid-forge's first functional release, and has a known unresolved kernel hang on real scan/connect -- intentionally left out of this database until it is validated end to end.

problemasConocidos.descripcion: IpClient tracks its interface by kernel ifindex, not by name. A manual `svc wifi disable`/`enable` toggle mid-session can race jg_netfix.sh's eth0->wlan0 rename against IpClient's own provisioning start for that connect attempt, leaving DNS/default-route unpopulated (observed once even stuck on "Wifi is disabled"). A clean container restart does not hit this. Pre-existing bug shared with the project's own jg-dashboard/pvz2-tv production use of the same HAL; not introduced or newly fixed by this module.

hwsim radios are claimed from a host-wide shared pool. Concurrent instances are coordinated within redroid-forge, but not against other, separate projects on the same host also using hwsim (e.g. jg-dashboard) -- that cross-project race is a known, deferred issue.
